concerns.text: The plan relies on synthetic fMRI data generated from noise estimates of real datasets. While this enables controlled effect sizes, it may not capture the full spatial, temporal, and physiological complexity of authentic BOLD signals, limiting the external validity of the resulting power curves for real‑world studies.

Replication success is defined with an arbitrary ±20 % magnitude tolerance relative to the known ground‑truth effect size. No justification or sensitivity analysis for this threshold is provided, and the choice could substantially bias estimated power.

Only 50 bootstrap iterations per configuration are planned. For low effect sizes this may yield unstable empirical replication probabilities and wide confidence intervals; a larger number of iterations (e.g., ≥ 200) is typically recommended for reliable power estimation.

The design assumes orthogonal predictors (sample size, smoothing kernel, SNR), yet SNR levels are derived from the same datasets used to simulate effect sizes, potentially inducing collinearity. VIF monitoring is mentioned but no explicit strategy to decorrelate these variables is described.

The cited OpenNeuro resources are parquet shards (e.g., `https://huggingface.co/datasets/clane9/openneuro-fslr64k/…/test-00000-of-00016.parquet`) that contain only curated BIDS metadata, not the raw NIfTI fMRI volumes required for ROI extraction, GLM fitting, and realistic noise estimation. Using these files as the primary fMRI data makes the dataset inappropriate for the intended statistical power analysis, which relies on voxel‑wise BOLD time‑series. Replace the citations with URLs to the full OpenNeuro BIDS datasets (e.g., the original `https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds000030` download) or ensure the referenced resources include the complete functional imaging files.

The plan’s Constitution Check states “Only the three URLs listed in the “Verified datasets” block are used,” but the research.md “Verified datasets” block lists five dataset URLs. This contradicts Principle II (Verified Accuracy) of the constitution, which requires the plan to accurately reflect the verified dataset sources.

The definition of `replication_success` (Section 3 ‘Statistical Approach’) requires the test‑set effect size to be within ±20 % of the *known ground‑truth* effect size (`target_effect_size`). The same `target_effect_size` is later used as a predictor in the logistic regression model (FR‑005). This makes the outcome variable directly dependent on one of its predictors, violating the independence requirement of split‑sample validation (Principle VI) and creating a circular/tautological validation where larger effect sizes trivially increase the probability of success.
